verses.1: And while Apollon was in Corinth, Paul went to the upper parts of that city to find some disciples.
verses.2: He also said to them, “Do you believe that it’s a holy spirit?” They replied, “We don’t know whether it’s really a holy spirit or not.”
verses.3: He also said, “In what place then did you baptize?” They replied, “In the baptism of John.”
verses.4: Paul said, “John baptized with water as a symbol of repentance. He did this so that the people would believe in Him who was coming after him. This is what happened to Jesus.”
verses.5: But when they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.6: And when the hands of Paul were touched by them, the holy spirit came upon them. He spoke in languages and gave them revelations from God.
verses.7: And all of these men were twelve in number.
verses.8: When he entered the assembly, he spent three months discussing and trying to persuade people about the kingdom of God.
verses.9: When some of them became stubborn and began to criticize the path ahead in front of the crowd, he dismissed those students from his presence. Every day, he continued to teach in Tyrus’s school.
verses.10: This happened after two years, so that all the people living in Asia could hear the words of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.11: Not only did the forces themselves, but also God created them through Paul’s hands.
verses.12: So that those who are weak can be freed from the harmful effects of lead and other toxic substances, and their diseases can be cured. Also, all those evil spirits can be driven away.
verses.13: Some of the Jewish believers also tried to accuse those who possessed evil spirits, by calling them “followers of Jesus”. They said, “We accuse you of following Jesus, whom Paul has proclaimed.”
verses.14: There were also seven sons of a Jewish high priest by some kind of woman.
verses.15: And when the evil spirit spoke, it said to them, “I know Jesus and I also know Paul. But who are you?”
verses.16: And when the man saw that there was a evil spirit within them, he tried to overpower it with his own strength. As a result, those who were naked and injured were able to escape from his house.
verses.17: This became known to both the Jews and the Greeks who lived in Ephesus. Fear spread among all of them. The name of Lord Jesus became very famous at that time.
verses.18: Many of those who were arrested also admitted their actions and disclosed what they had done.
verses.19: And those who were capable of governing in times of crisis gathered together and read the books before everyone else. They also decided on their own rewards, and they found five silver coins as payment.
verses.20: In this way, according to the will of the Lord, the word became powerful and effective.
verses.21: When all these things were fulfilled, Paul decided to travel through Macedonia and Achaia towards Jerusalem. He said that after what had happened there, he also wanted to see Jerusalem.
verses.22: And since you sent two of those who served him to Makedonia, Timotheus and Erastus, he himself spent some time in Asia.
verses.23: And in those times, there were quite a few disruptions along that route.
verses.24: Demetrios, for example, was called “Silver Collector”. He was responsible for producing silver vessels for Artemis. This task required a great deal of effort from the craftsmen.
verses.25: And when you gathered those who were involved in these tasks together, you said, “Men, be aware that from this work, our wealth comes.”
verses.26: And you should also consider and hear that not only Eusebius, but almost all of Asia, was convinced by Paul’s teachings. He said that there are no gods who are created by human hands.
verses.27: Not only does this pose a risk to us in terms of being condemned, but also the temple of the great goddess Artemis may be completely destroyed. Its greatness, which is respected by all of Asia and its inhabitants, will also be lost.
verses.28: When they heard this and became filled with anger, they said, “Arteemis is a great city in Ephesus.”
verses.29: And the city was affected by this situation. The people became united and rushed to the theater, along with Gaius and Aristarchus from the Maecenas family, who had brought Paul’s relics with them.
verses.30: But Paul wanted to go into the crowd, but his disciples did not allow him to do so.
verses.31: And even some of the emperors of Asia, who were his friends, sent messages to him, asking that he not be allowed to go to the theater.
verses.32: Others, however, did something else. After all, the church was scattered over a wide area, and most people didn’t know why they had been forced to leave.
verses.33: From the crowd, Alexander was surrounded by those who opposed him among the Jews. But Alexander, after shaking his hand, wanted to apologize to the people.
verses.34: Knowing that he was a Jew, a voice arose from among all of them, after two hours. It was the great Artephius of Ephesus.
verses.35: And the clerk ordered the crowd to stop. He said, “Men of Ephesus, who among you doesn’t know that Ephesus is a city that was built by the great Artemis, and by the sun god?”
verses.36: Therefore, in the face of those who resist this, it is necessary for you to remain calm and not do anything rash.
verses.37: For you have brought these men here, neither as priests nor as those who blaspheme our God.
verses.38: If Demetrius and those who are with him indeed have some reason for their actions, then they must be considered as people who are willing to go through any lengths to achieve their goals. They’ve even called each other “friends”.
verses.39: If you have any further questions, they will be addressed in the regulations of the assembly.
verses.40: And indeed, we risk being accused of being stubborn in the face of any reason that might be presented today. We certainly cannot accept such accusations regarding this conflict. Having said this, he dismissed the assembly.
